main_text.p: 5. Non satis perpendunt, bona temporaria & succesfus improbis in malum cedere. Psal.69.22. Sit mensa eorum ipsis pro laqueo, & illorum prospera pro reti.

6. Verisimum esse Nazianzeni dictu: Nemo vires suas in pace cognoscit: si enim bella desunt, virtutum experimenta non prosunt. non satis perpendunt. Alioquin virtutem in fide & caritate per adversa illustrari, animaduerterent.

Etsi autè dulcisimè dicitur: Pietas ad omnia utilis est, ut quæ promisfiones habeat vitæ prꝗsentis & futuræ: 1. Tim. 4.8. Item: Timete Iehova Sancti eius: quia nihil deest timetibus eum: Psal. 34.9. acualde jucunda sunt exempla Iosephi & Dauidis & Danielis, e gurgitibus malorum emergētium, & ad summos honorum & gloriæ gradus eue&torum: tamen nunquā crux a pietate & veritate separanda erat, tantisper donec fideles in hoc mundo militat. Nam & ista verè dicitur: Omnes qui volent piè viuere in Christo Iesu, persecutionem patientur: 2. Tim. 3.12. Item: Multa sunt adversa iustis, sed ex ijs omnibus liberat unusquisq; eorum Iehovah: Psal. 34.19. Et experti sunt Sancti illi viri, quorum memi-

page.notes: The reference "Psal.34.19." is split across the line end; the "19." is set slightly larger at the start of the last line, so it is joined here. The printed "ni-hil" and "dulcisimè", "prꝗsentis" (with ꝗ-type abbreviation for præ, read with some doubt), and "eue&torum" (probably evectorum, printed with an ampersand) are kept as printed. "Verisimum" is kept as printed. "iucunda" is given with consonant j per the orthography rule. The catchword "memi-" is the start of the next page's first word and keeps its printed hyphen.
